name: A Reference Java Microservices Banking Sample — Accounts Domain (frontend + userservice + contacts + accounts-db)
description: Hand-authored gold CALM for a real, wild-type reference Java microservices banking sample's accounts bounded context (a real public multi-service reference repo, local clone at spikes/refbank/repo). Deliberately well-connected — authored specifically to give Weaver a real, non-trivial multi-service architecture to test against, after an earlier review found several hand-authored lab-fixture gold packages had disconnected nodes. Every node, route, relationship, and control below is grep-verified against real source and real k8s manifests, cited at file:line — none inferred from README/docs/diagrams (this repo's own gold-authoring rule, gold/calm/README.md).

nodes.name: Bank customer
nodes.description: A customer using the web UI to log in, sign up, view contacts, and make payments/deposits.

nodes.name: Frontend
nodes.description: Flask BFF (backend-for-frontend) serving server-rendered HTML and orchestrating calls to userservice/contacts/ledger services on the user's behalf (src/frontend/frontend.py). Not a browser SPA — a real server-side Flask app, hence node-type service, not webclient.

security-auth-001.description: Token-based authentication (call-site, unverified enforcement elsewhere) — real, precise nuance: frontend.py has TWO jwt.decode call sites with genuinely different security meaning. decode_token() (L616-619) sets verify_signature: False — reads claims only, no enforcement. verify_token() (L621, jwt.decode call itself at L629-632) sets verify_signature: True with the real public key — this IS the genuine enforcement call. Citing the verifying one as the control evidence; the non-verifying one is real code but NOT security evidence, named here so it isn't confused for enforcement by a future reader or a future Weaver detection pass.

nodes.name: User Service
nodes.description: Flask service managing user account creation and login; issues signed JWTs on successful login (src/accounts/userservice/userservice.py).

security-auth-jwt-issue-001.description: Issues RS256-signed session JWTs on successful login, using the private key half of the k8s Secret 'jwt-key' (mounted read-only at /tmp/.ssh/privatekey per kubernetes-manifests/userservice.yaml). No CALM-generator catalogue row exists for token-ISSUANCE specifically (only decode/verify is currently catalogued) — a real, named coverage gap surfaced by authoring this gold, not by inspecting Weaver's code.

nodes.name: Contacts Service
nodes.description: Flask service managing a user's linked payee/contact accounts, gating both read and write on a verified JWT (src/accounts/contacts/contacts.py).

security-auth-001.description: Token-based authentication (call-site, unverified enforcement) — both the GET and POST /contacts/{username} handlers call jwt.decode with the shared public key before touching contacts_db, and additionally check the decoded 'user' claim matches the requested :username path segment (a real authorization check layered on top of authentication, not just token validity).

nodes.name: Accounts Database
nodes.description: Real, single PostgreSQL StatefulSet shared by both userservice and contacts (kubernetes-manifests/accounts-db.yaml) — both services connect via the SAME ACCOUNTS_DB_URI (postgresql://accounts-admin:...@accounts-db:5432/accounts-db, from the shared 'accounts-db-config' ConfigMap). Deliberately modeled as ONE deployable-unit node, not two — UserDb (userservice/db.py) and ContactsDb (contacts/db.py) are application-level SQLAlchemy wrapper classes inside each service's own codebase, not separate deployable data stores; collapsing to the real physical database matches this project's own 'node = deployable unit, not class' discipline. If Weaver's own generated output shows two separate database nodes here, that is a real, meaningful grain difference worth surfacing, not a bug in this gold file.

nodes.name: A Reference Java Microservices Banking Sample — Accounts Domain
nodes.description: Logical domain composition — the accounts bounded context, composed-of below.

nodes.name: Reference Sample Kubernetes Cluster (accounts domain)
nodes.description: Runtime placement boundary. In this real repo composed-of and deployed-in happen to name the same four nodes (all genuinely run in the same real cluster, per kubernetes-manifests/*.yaml) — a real case where the two questions have the same answer, not a modeling shortcut; see coe-lab/docs/reference/how-to-capture-architecture-in-calm.md Step 4 for when they diverge instead.

relationships.description: Customer loads pages and submits login/signup/payment/deposit forms.

Frontend calls userservice's /login and /users endpoints — app.config['LOGIN_URI']/['USERSERVICE_URI'] are built from the real USERSERVICE_API_ADDR env var (frontend.py:663-666), which the shared 'environment-config' ConfigMap sets to the literal value "userservice:8080" (kubernetes-manifests/config.yaml).

Frontend calls contacts's /contacts/{username} endpoint — app.config['CONTACTS_URI'] is built from the real CONTACTS_API_ADDR env var (frontend.py:672-673), set to the literal value "contacts:8080" by the same shared ConfigMap.
userservice's UserDb class opens a real SQLAlchemy engine against ACCOUNTS_DB_URI (userservice/db.py:31) to read/write the users table.
contacts's ContactsDb class opens a real SQLAlchemy engine against the same ACCOUNTS_DB_URI (contacts/db.py:31) to read/write the contacts table.
The accounts domain is composed of these four real deployable units (excludes the actor, external to the system).
All four are real Kubernetes workloads in kubernetes-manifests/{frontend,userservice,contacts,accounts-db}.yaml (Deployment/Deployment/Deployment/StatefulSet respectively).

metadata.value: a real public multi-service reference repo (local clone: spikes/refbank/repo)

Solid, well-connected reference gold to test the Weaver pipeline against — authored after a review found several existing lab-fixture gold packages had disconnected nodes (missing same-package connects edges); see coe-lab/docs/findings/gold-calm-relationship-connectivity-audit.md for that finding.

userservice, contacts, and frontend all mount the SAME k8s Secret 'jwt-key' (userservice mounts both jwtRS256.key + jwtRS256.key.pub; contacts and frontend mount only jwtRS256.key.pub) — kubernetes-manifests/{userservice,contacts,frontend}.yaml, secretName: jwt-key. This is a real, config-mediated trust relationship (shared signing-key material), NOT a network connects edge — no direct network call between userservice and contacts exists (confirmed: neither service's source references the other's API_ADDR). CALM has no first-class 'shares-secret'/'trust' relationship-type, so this is deliberately captured via each node's own security-auth-* control + this metadata note rather than fabricating a connects edge that would misrepresent real network traffic. This is the exact fact CLAUDE.md's own x-aac-scope-limitations names as something Weaver has never detected end-to-end.

userservice-to-accounts-db and contacts-to-accounts-db deliberately have NO protocol value. Both connections are SQLAlchemy-over-psycopg2 talking real PostgreSQL wire protocol — CALM's protocol enum (HTTP/HTTPS/FTP/SFTP/JDBC/WebSocket/SocketIO/LDAP/AMQP/TLS/mTLS/TCP) has no honest value for this: JDBC is literally Java Database Connectivity, a Java-ecosystem-specific term, and would misrepresent a Python connection if used. Same enum-gap class already found for Kafka in coe-lab/docs/reference/rich-calm-example/README.md #2.2 — this is a second, independently-confirmed real instance of the same finding, from a real repo rather than a synthetic example.
